newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi urges private sector to hire more nationals.
newsitem.headline: Saudi urges private sector to hire more nationals.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's commerce minister has urged the private sector to hire more Saudi nationals and train youths for jobs, Saudi newspapers said on Thursday.
Only an estimated seven percent of private sector employees in the kingdom are Saudi nationals. About five million expatriates work in Saudi Arabia, which has a population of around 18 million.

"(The private sector) should take appropriate measures for their (nationals') training and rehabilitation," said Commerce Minister Osama bin Jaafar bin Ibrahim Faqih, as quoted by the English-language daily Arab News.
He added that Saudi youths "should work sincerely for the service of their country".

Saudi Arabia's 1995-2000 development plan sets a target of creating 659,900 jobs for Saudis by the end of the century. Some 319,500 expatriate workers are to be gradually phased out of the workforce to make room for Saudi citizens.

In October, Riyadh banned expatriates from 14 types of job and said existing work permits for the prohibited professions would not be renewed. The jobs range from personnel officers to treasurers, auctioneers and security guards.
